items.definition:
the part of the brain involved in memory formation
Damage to the hippocampus can severely impair long-term memory.

a system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters
Renaissance humanism emphasized the potential for human achievement.

the process of taking food, drink, or another substance into the body by swallowing or absorbing it
Proper ingestion of nutrients is vital for health.

the state of being confined as a prisoner, especially for political or military reasons
During the war, many foreign nationals faced internment.

a huge, powerful, and overwhelming force or institution
The company became a marketing juggernaut, dominating the industry.

The process of maturing.
The maturation of the fruit takes several weeks.

A shiny silicate mineral with a layered structure.
Mica is often used in cosmetics for its shimmering effect.

The action of bothering or annoying someone; sexual abuse.
The law protects individuals from molestation.

a person who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves
He was such a narcissist that he couldn't stop looking at his own reflection.

a medical condition in which the bones become brittle and fragile
Regular exercise can help prevent osteoporosis in older adults.

a large, imposing building, especially in Italy
The family lived in a grand palazzo overlooking the canal.

a queen or princess in India
The rani wore a magnificent sari adorned with jewels.

a flowing back or return flow
He suffers from acid reflux after eating spicy food.

the action of restoring someone or something to their former position or state
The union demanded the reinstatement of the fired workers.

a small mammal; black or dark brown color
She wore a luxurious coat of sable fur.

a state of inactivity or equilibrium
The project remained in a state of stasis due to lack of funding.

a wall made of stones; an act of obstruction or uncooperativeness
The committee faced a stonewall from the uncooperative witness.

a departure from what is normal, usual, or expected
His outburst was an aberration from his usual calm behavior.

a person who settles a dispute or has ultimate authority in a matter
The judge acted as an arbiter in the dispute.

the physical qualities that are characteristic of athletes
His athleticism was evident in every movement on the field.

a compound of carbon with a more electropositive element
Tungsten carbide is used in cutting tools.

a vivid crimson color
The painting featured a rich carmine hue.

the process of managing or running something for commercial gain
The commercialization of the internet changed everything.

the process by which heat or electricity is directly transmitted through a substance
Heat conduction is efficient in metals.

the protection or promotion of the interests of consumers; the preoccupation with the acquisition of consumer goods
The rise of consumerism has led to increased waste.

the science of the origin and development of the universe
She is studying cosmology to understand the universe.

a list of cases for trial or things to be done; a document summarizing a case
The judge reviewed the court docket for the day.

a band or bundle of fibrous connective tissue; a dashboard or front panel of a vehicle
The car's fascia was damaged in the accident, requiring replacement.

a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and constituent political units
Federalism allows for both national unity and regional diversity in governance.

a shaped piece of material used to seal the junction between two surfaces
The mechanic replaced the faulty gasket in the engine to stop the leak.

the act of living in a place; a place of residence
The old cabin showed signs of recent habitation, despite its remote location.

an enterprising person, or someone who obtains money dishonestly
He was known as a street hustler, always looking for a deal.

the examination or observation of one's own mental and emotional processes
He spent time in quiet introspection, reflecting on his life choices.

the amount of freedom to move or act
The manager gave us some leeway to finish the project.

a French title or form of address for an unmarried woman
The waiter addressed her as Mademoiselle.

a synthetic opioid used as a pain reliever and in the treatment of opioid addiction
Methadone is often used in medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder.

a poisonous liquid alcohol
Methanol is used as a solvent and as a fuel.

an extinct flightless bird native to New Zealand
The moa was a large, flightless bird that once roamed New Zealand.

the release of an egg from the ovary
Ovulation typically occurs once a month in fertile women.

a knight renowned for heroism and chivalry
In the story, the paladin bravely defended the innocent villagers.

the working class
Marx wrote extensively about the struggles of the proletariat.

a stock of plays, dances, or pieces that a company or performer knows or is prepared to perform
The theater company has a wide repertory of classical plays.

a man who pursues a relationship with a woman, often with the aim of marriage
She had many suitors vying for her attention.

the whole of something
During the eclipse, the moon reached totality, completely blocking the sun.

The wasting away of a body organ or tissue.
Prolonged disuse can lead to muscle atrophy.

A huge or monstrous creature; something enormous.
The new skyscraper was a concrete behemoth dominating the skyline.

A member of the majority faction of the Russian Social Democratic Party, which seized power in the October Revolution of 1917.
The Bolsheviks played a crucial role in the Russian Revolution.

A pirate, especially one who preyed on Spanish ships in the Caribbean in the 17th century.
The buccaneer buried his treasure on a deserted island.

The first geological period of the Paleozoic Era, lasting from 541 to 485.4 million years ago.
Many new forms of life appeared during the Cambrian explosion.

mercy; lenience.
The prisoner appealed to the governor for clemency.

a police force covering a particular area.
The local constabulary responded quickly to the incident.

the study of how to arrange reproduction within a human population to increase the occurrence of heritable characteristics regarded as desirable
The history of eugenics is controversial and often associated with unethical practices.

an exact copy, especially of written or printed material
The museum displayed a facsimile of the original manuscript.

a colorless pungent gas, used in solution as a disinfectant and preservative
Formaldehyde is used in many industrial processes.

a complex geometric pattern that is self-similar across different scales
The coastline often exhibits fractal properties.

a very small amount
There wasn't an iota of doubt in her mind.

an adherent of jihad
The government is working to counter the threat posed by jihadist groups.

a gentle sheen or soft glow, especially that of a partly reflective surface
The antique furniture had lost its original lustre.

the plural of maximum; points at which a function's value is greatest
The graph shows several local maxima and minima.

the absence of anything; nonexistence
He stared into the vast nothingness of the night sky.

miscellaneous articles, especially the equipment needed for a particular activity
The magician laid out all his paraphernalia on the table.

a chemical obtained from petroleum and natural gas
The company specializes in the production of petrochemicals.

a tough, light, flexible synthetic resin made by polymerizing ethylene, chiefly used for plastic bags, containers, and other packaging
Most plastic bags are made from polyethylene.

all future generations of people
We must preserve these documents for posterity.
